entries.geometryVintage: Census 2000 voting districts (VTD); 2000 Amendment 2 returns crosswalked onto 2000 VTD geometry (1,987 VTDs)
entries.source: Alabama Secretary of State 2000 general-election county precinct workbooks (66 workbooks, including the separately parsed Jefferson and Walker sources); returns crosswalked onto Census 2000 VTD geography

results.note: Published analytical VTD table: one row per Census 2000 VTD with the allocated Yes/No votes; the GeoPackage carries the same allocation.

entries.matchMethod: 2006 Agriculture Commissioner tiered method: county-constrained exact VTD code, exact normalized polling-place name, multi-evidence scoring (independent partisan fingerprint, turnout capacity, Black VAP share), reviewed alias tables and many-to-one aggregation of county reporting boxes.
entries.sourceTotalsNote: Certified statewide totals include absentee and provisional ballots that are not assignable to a VTD (24,184 Yes and 13,695 No votes); 1,772 of the 1,987 Census 2000 VTDs carry a recovered reporting unit and the remaining 215 VTDs have no recoverable Amendment 2 boxes.
entries.unmatchedFix: Every source reporting box is assigned to a VTD; absent and unassignable ballots are reported in render-audit.json rather than matched by the editor.

entries.geometryVintage: Census 2000 voting districts (VTD); 2000 presidential returns allocated onto the same 1,987-VTD geometry as Amendment 2
entries.source: Alabama 2000 certified presidential returns parsed from the county precinct workbooks and allocated with the same reviewed 2000 VTD crosswalk used for Amendment 2; major-party votes only

results.note: Analytical allocation of the 2000 presidential returns: gore_allocated and bush_allocated per Census 2000 VTD. The published render layer merges same-place VTD fragments and fills 197 units with a nearest same-county display margin; those inferred colors are not votes and are not loaded here.

entries.matchMethod: Same reviewed 2000 VTD crosswalk as the Amendment 2 reconstruction: 2,608 presidential source rows were allocated onto 1,987 Census 2000 VTDs with zero unmatched allocation units; 1,772 VTDs carry allocated votes and 197 render units show a nearest same-county display margin that is explicitly excluded from the loaded votes.
entries.sourceTotalsNote: Certified statewide totals; 28,987 Gore and 40,643 Bush votes (absentee, provisional and federal-only ballots) are not assignable to a VTD, and the 32,488 votes for other candidates are not distributed to precincts.
entries.unmatchedFix: The allocation audit records zero unmatched presidential source units; unassignable absentee and provisional ballots are reported in render-audit.json instead of being matched by the editor.

entries.geometryVintage: Census 2000 voting districts (VTD); 2006 county reporting units crosswalked onto 2000 VTD geometry (1,987 VTDs). No official November 2006 precinct boundary file exists for Alabama
entries.source: Alabama 2006 general-election county precinct workbooks (Agriculture Commissioner contest); reconstructed and audited 2006-to-2000 VTD crosswalk with reviewed alias, geocoded and iterative tiers

results.note: Published analytical VTD table: one row per Census 2000 VTD with the allocated Sparks/Lipscomb votes.

entries.matchMethod: County-constrained 2006-to-2000 VTD reconstruction: exact VTD code, exact normalized polling-place name, multi-evidence scoring (other-contest fingerprint, Black VAP share, ballots-to-VAP plausibility), reviewed relocation aliases, geocoded historical addresses and residual optimizer tiers. Unresolved returns are never forced onto a polygon.
entries.sourceTotalsLabel: Recovered reporting-box totals from 66 counties, not certified statewide totals
entries.sourceTotalsNote: Sum of all 2,263 source reporting boxes in precinct-crosswalk-audit.csv (the 66 county workbooks): the accepted 2,250 boxes carry 678,218 Sparks votes and 469,269 Lipscomb votes onto 1,746 of the 1,987 VTDs. Absentee and provisional ballots and the missing Coosa County agriculture-commissioner contest are outside precinct geography.
entries.unmatchedFix: The 13 unassigned source boxes (Butler, Calhoun, Conecuh, DeKalb, Hale, Lawrence, Lee, Russell, Shelby) are listed with their votes in precinct-crosswalk-audit.csv as needs-review. Assign them upstream and regenerate the crosswalk; the editor never re-matches precinct names.

entries.source: VEST 2017 Alabama precinct returns and boundaries

entries.geometryVintage: 2024 statewide election precinct layer (congressional-split derivative, 1,979 features); 2026 returns joined onto 2024 precinct polygons
entries.source: Alabama Secretary of State 2026 primary county workbooks; every 2026 polling-place return matched to a 2024 precinct polygon by the shared reviewed 2026 crosswalk

results.note: Published 2026 result polygons: one row per 2024 precinct polygon with the four Democratic Senate candidates, winner and match score. Rows flagged matched=false are 2024 polygons that received no standalone 2026 return.

entries.matchMethod: Shared 2026 return-to-2024-precinct crosswalk applied identically to both party contests: verified polling-place aliases and relocations from Alabama CD-5, exact and high-confidence normalized labels, unique official precinct numbers, county change notices and polling lists, geocoded current addresses, and a reviewed nearest-polygon assignment for renamed locations. Absentee and provisional labels are excluded from geography, and Jefferson precincts 3010 and 3015 form one 2026 reporting unit.
entries.sourceTotalsNote: Official statewide Democratic primary totals from the county workbooks; absentee and provisional ballots are not assignable to precinct geography.
entries.unmatchedFix: The Jefferson PREC 3010/3015 combined 2026 reporting unit covers two separate 2024 polygons. Its votes remain in totals without a fabricated polygon. The existing custom 2026 analytical layer merges this unit, but its all-precinct keys differ from these published congressional-split result keys; it is not substituted silently.
